newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebels give Zaire army generals deadline to disarm.
newsitem.headline: Rebels give Zaire army generals deadline to disarm.

text.p: Rebels fighting to overthrow Zaire's government said on Monday they had given government army generals a deadline of March 13 to lay down their weapons.

"No harm will come to them at all if they disarm, and we appeal to them to do so and avoid spilling inocent blood on Zairean soil," Moise Nyarugabo, secretary-general at rebel headquarters in the eastern border city of Goma told Reuters.
The appeal was also broadcast on rebel-controlled local radio.

The Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL) has taken over a 1,000 km (600 mile) long chunk of land stretching deep into Zaire since launching their rebellion in October.
The avowed aim of the rebels, led by veteran opponent Laurent Kabila, is to topple president Mobutu Sese Seko, who has ruled Zaire for 31 years and is now ailing in France.
"Mobutu's army must realise it is over and we should head for a peaceful settlement to the war, we have now captured Kindu and will soon be in Kisangani," said Nyarugabo.

Kisangani is the largest city in eastern Zaie and has been the main base for a Zaire army counter-offensive, mounted with the help of foreign mercenaries, which has failed to turn back the rebel advance.

The ADFL claims to have captured Kindu, 400 km (250 miles) from the eastern border, at the weekend. The Kinshasa government says its forces still hold Kindu and dismisses rebel claims as propaganda intended to cause panic.
"Kisangani is the last card the army has to play, but they will be defeated there as they have been everywhere else," Nyarugabo said.
